project.name: captcha-pro
project.description: A lightweight, framework-agnostic behavioral captcha library (slider, click, invisible, popup) delivered as a pnpm + Turborepo monorepo across 10+ platforms (Web/Vue2/Vue3/React/WeChat/uni-app/Taro/Flutter/Android/iOS)

nodes.name: click.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the ClickCaptcha class, a canvas-based click-point verification captcha that generates random character targets on a noisy background and validates user click positions against them.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses dual-canvas rendering (background + text overlay) with HTML image generation for click target prompts.

nodes.name: index.default.ts
nodes.summary: Barrel file re-exporting the full public API of the core package for default import consumers.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure re-export module with no logic — all 14 exports are pass-through from index.ts.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Main package entry point that re-exports all captcha classes, types, i18n functions, and provides factory functions for creating each captcha type.
nodes.languageNotes: Factory functions (createSliderCaptcha, createClickCaptcha, etc.) are thin wrappers that instantiate captcha classes with provided options.

nodes.name: invisible.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the InvisibleCaptcha class, which monitors user behavioral signals (mouse movement, touch patterns, click timing) to calculate a risk score and optionally presents a fallback challenge.
nodes.languageNotes: Integrates generateFingerprint and calculateBehaviorScore from utils for device fingerprinting and behavioral analysis.

nodes.name: en-US.ts
nodes.summary: English locale message bundle providing UI strings for captcha prompts, success, and error states.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Internationalization module providing locale management, translation lookup (t), message retrieval, and browser locale detection across supported languages.
nodes.languageNotes: Exposes an i18n object aggregating all locale functions for convenient re-export.

nodes.name: zh-CN.ts
nodes.summary: Simplified Chinese locale message bundle providing UI strings for captcha prompts, success, and error states.

nodes.name: popup.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the PopupCaptcha class, which wraps any captcha type in a modal popup with overlay, close button, ESC key support, and focus management for accessibility.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses injectPopupStyles for CSS injection and delegates to slider/click captcha instances for the actual challenge.

nodes.name: slider.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the SliderCaptcha class, a canvas-based slider puzzle captcha with multiple piece shapes (rounded rect, triangle, trapezoid, pentagon), decoy holes, noise textures, and drag-to-verify mechanics.
nodes.languageNotes: Most complex module — 36 methods including shape drawing, slider piece generation, dual-canvas compositing, and both frontend/backend verification paths.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Core type definitions for all captcha options, instances, data structures, backend verification, security, and statistics interfaces used across the package.
nodes.languageNotes: Defines BaseCaptchaOptions, CaptchaInstance, CaptchaData, SecurityOptions, and per-captcha option interfaces (SliderCaptchaOptions, ClickCaptchaOptions, etc.).

nodes.name: utils.ts
nodes.summary: Shared utility library providing DOM helpers, canvas drawing, AES encryption/decryption, signature generation, device fingerprinting, behavioral scoring, HTTP requests, and CSS injection for the captcha system.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Web Crypto API (subtle.encrypt/decrypt) for AES-GCM encryption and derives keys via PBKDF2.

nodes.name: ClickCaptcha
nodes.summary: Canvas-based click-point captcha that generates target characters on a noisy background, tracks user clicks, and verifies points against targets with optional backend verification and signed data support.
nodes.languageNotes: 31 methods spanning rendering, point generation, overlap detection, char image generation, event handling, frontend/backend verification, and statistics.

nodes.name: InvisibleCaptcha
nodes.summary: Behavioral captcha that passively monitors mouse, touch, and click interactions to compute a risk score, triggering a visible challenge only when risk is high.
nodes.languageNotes: 18 methods including startMonitoring/stopMonitoring for event lifecycle, calculateRisk for scoring, and showChallenge/hideChallenge for fallback UI.

nodes.name: PopupCaptcha
nodes.summary: Modal wrapper that encapsulates any captcha type in an accessible popup with overlay, ESC key dismissal, focus management, and success/fail callback delegation.
nodes.languageNotes: 9 methods managing popup lifecycle (createPopup, show, hide, destroy) and captcha delegation (createCaptcha, getCaptcha).

nodes.name: SliderCaptcha
nodes.summary: Canvas-based slider puzzle captcha with randomized piece shapes, decoy holes, noise textures, drag-to-verify mechanics, and both frontend and backend verification paths.
nodes.languageNotes: 36 methods including shape rendering (drawTriangle, drawTrapezoid, drawPentagon, drawRoundedRect), slider piece generation with clipping, and drag event handling.

nodes.name: deriveAesKey
nodes.summary: Derives an AES encryption key from a secret key and salt using the Web Crypto API's PBKDF2 key derivation.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses crypto.subtle.importKey and deriveBits for PBKDF2-based key derivation.

nodes.name: aesEncrypt
nodes.summary: Encrypts plaintext using AES-GCM with a derived key, returning a base64-encoded ciphertext bundle containing IV, salt, and encrypted data.
nodes.languageNotes: Combines random IV and salt generation with AES-GCM encryption via crypto.subtle.encrypt.

nodes.name: aesDecrypt
nodes.summary: Decrypts a base64-encoded AES-GCM ciphertext bundle (IV + salt + encrypted data) using a derived key, returning the plaintext string.
nodes.languageNotes: Splits the combined buffer into IV, salt, and ciphertext, then decrypts via crypto.subtle.decrypt.

nodes.name: generateEncryptedData

nodes.name: decryptCaptchaData

nodes.name: generateSignature
nodes.summary: Generates a cryptographic signature for captcha verification data by encrypting the payload with a secret key, used for backend verification integrity.

nodes.name: generateFingerprint
nodes.summary: Generates a browser fingerprint by combining screen properties, timezone, language, platform, and user agent characteristics into a hashed numeric identifier.
nodes.languageNotes: Collects navigator, screen, and Date timezone data, then hashes the concatenated components into a numeric fingerprint.

nodes.name: calculateBehaviorScore
nodes.summary: Analyzes user interaction tracks (mouse movements, touch paths, click timing) to produce a behavioral risk score between 0 and 1, factoring in velocity, acceleration, angle consistency, and timing patterns.
nodes.languageNotes: Computes Euclidean distances, angular changes, and acceleration to detect bot-like patterns in interaction data.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The README introduces captcha-pro as a lightweight, framework-agnostic behavioral captcha library supporting slider puzzle, click verification, invisible captcha, and popup mode across 10+ platforms. It documents the two verification modes (frontend-only and backend-verified), the quick-start installation, and the multi-platform package matrix. This is the roadmap for the tour ahead — each subsequent step traces one layer of the architecture described here.

tour.title: Core Library Entry Point
tour.description: The core package barrel (packages/core/src/index.ts) is the most depended-upon file in the entire monorepo with a fan-in of 12. It re-exports all captcha classes, types, and i18n functions, and provides factory functions (createSliderCaptcha, createClickCaptcha, etc.) that every platform binding imports. Starting here reveals the public API surface that the rest of the codebase is built upon.
tour.languageLesson: TypeScript barrel files use 'export * from' to re-export modules, creating a clean public API surface. Factory functions here are thin wrappers that instantiate captcha classes with provided options, allowing consumers to import either a class or a factory.

tour.title: Core Types & Utilities
tour.description: Building on the barrel from Step 2, the types.ts and utils.ts files form the foundational vocabulary of the library. types.ts defines the captcha configuration interfaces, verification result types, and point/position types used across every platform binding (fan-in of 5 each). utils.ts provides the shared logic — fingerprint generation, behavioral scoring, canvas helpers — that the captcha classes depend on.

tour.title: Captcha Implementations
tour.description: These four files are the heart of the library and form the largest tightly coupled cluster in the graph. slider.ts is the most complex module (36 methods for shape drawing, dual-canvas compositing, and frontend/backend verification), click.ts generates random character targets on a noisy background, invisible.ts monitors behavioral signals for risk scoring, and popup.ts wraps any captcha type in an accessible modal. Together they implement the four captcha modes the README describes.

tour.title: Internationalization System
tour.description: The locales module (fan-in of 4) provides locale management, translation lookup, and browser detection across supported languages. It aggregates the en-US and zh-CN message bundles that supply UI strings for captcha prompts, success, and error states. This i18n layer is consumed by both the core captcha classes and the platform SDKs, ensuring consistent multi-language support across every platform.

tour.title: Web Framework SDKs
tour.description: The web-sdk layer wraps the core library for Vue 3 and React applications. The Vue package exposes composables (useSliderCaptcha, useClickCaptcha) that encapsulate captcha lifecycle logic, while the React package provides equivalent hooks. Both re-export the core API and register framework-specific components that render the canvas-based captcha from Step 4.
tour.languageLesson: Vue composables and React hooks serve the same architectural purpose: extracting reusable stateful logic from UI components. The Vue package uses the Composition API's ref/reactive, while the React package uses useState/useEffect, but both delegate to the same core captcha classes.

tour.title: Mini-Program SDKs
tour.description: The miniprogram layer adapts the core for WeChat, Taro, and uni-app runtimes that lack DOM and canvas APIs. The mp-shared package (fan-in of 4 for its request module) provides shared captcha logic, types, and constants across all mini-program variants. The WeChat package uses native wxml/wxss components, while Taro packages bridge to their respective framework runtimes.

tour.title: Native Mobile SDKs
tour.description: The native-sdk layer provides platform-specific captcha implementations for Android (Kotlin) and iOS (Swift). Android's CaptchaPro.kt serves as the main entry with a CaptchaGenerator and custom Views, while iOS uses Package.swift for SPM distribution with SwiftUI views and UIKit views. The Types.kt and Types.swift files (fan-in of 5 and 4 respectively) mirror the core types.ts contract from Step 3 in each platform's native language.
tour.languageLesson: Kotlin and Swift both use value types (data classes / structs) for domain models and protocol-oriented design for polymorphism. The Android SDK uses Jetpack Compose for declarative UI, while iOS uses SwiftUI — both frameworks mirror the React/Vue component pattern from Step 6.

tour.title: Backend Verification Services
tour.description: The server layer provides three independent backends (Node.js, Go, Java Spring Boot) that validate captcha tokens issued by client SDKs. Each implements image generation, AES-GCM encrypted token exchange, rate limiting, and brute-force protection. The Node.js server (fan-in of 5) is the reference implementation, while Go and Java provide idiomatic alternatives for different backend stacks.
tour.languageLesson: AES-GCM (Galois/Counter Mode) provides authenticated encryption — both confidentiality and integrity — making it ideal for captcha token exchange. The same algorithm is implemented across three languages to ensure cross-backend compatibility, each using the language's native crypto library.

tour.title: Example Applications
tour.description: The examples layer demonstrates SDK integration across platforms. The Vue and React examples (App.tsx has the highest fan-out at 12, importing all demo pages) showcase all four captcha types with backend verification demos. The HTML example shows vanilla JS CDN usage, and the WeChat mini-program example demonstrates the backend-only mode described in the README.

tour.title: Monorepo Infrastructure & CI/CD
tour.description: The tour closes with the monorepo tooling that orchestrates the entire codebase. Turbo.json defines cached build/test/dev tasks across all workspace packages, while pnpm-workspace.yaml declares the package and server directories. GitHub Actions pipelines handle CI (build, lint, code analysis) and CD (npm publishing on release), and the architecture docs document the layered design this tour has walked through.
tour.languageLesson: Turborepo uses content-hash-based caching and dependency-aware task scheduling to parallelize builds across monorepo packages. Tasks declare their inputs (outputs) so Turbo can skip rebuilding unchanged packages — a 10-package monorepo like this can cut CI build time by 60-80% with cache hits.
